outcome: Give logistics coo / supply chain director a governed method to improve truck dwell hours using truck check-ins, yard capacity and dock appointments, with final decisions retained by named staff.
overview: Yard Gate Appointment Management addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in logistics and supply chain operations. The first proof of value uses truck check-ins, yard capacity and dock appointments. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is truck dwell hours, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: truck check-ins, yard capacity and dock appointments; define truck dwell hours and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Logistics COO / Supply Chain Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for truck dwell hours
